external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of Halifax II BB216 (LQ:D) from 405 (Vancouver) Squadron RCAF. The aircraft took off from RAF Topcliffe at 2303 on 1 September 1942 for a bombing mission to Saarbrucken. After crossing the coast at 2344, the port outer engine caught fire; though the blaze was extinguished, structural failure of the port wing followed and the order to bail out was given. At least two airmen fell into the sea and drowned. The Halifax crashed at 2358 near Chapel St Leonards.
key_details: Pilot was Flt Sgt Norman Angus MacKenzie R86313 RCAF, age 27
Port outer engine fire led to port wing structural failure
At least two crew fell into the sea
Four killed: MacKenzie, Eagles (age 21), Stone (age 20), Dawdy (age 26)

memorial_details:
Name: Handley Page Halifax BB216
Type: Stone of remembrance
Description: Polished granite stone on a plinth, fixed onto a two stepped concrete base. Two wooden slatted planters either side and a vase in front.
Inscription: Stone: (405 Squadron RCAF badge)/ Just before Midnight/ on 1st September 1942/ HALIFAX II BB216 (LQ-D)/ of 405 Squadron RCAF/ from Topcliffe/ crashed near this spot/ following a disastrous engine fire/ This memorial is placed here to/ commemorate the crew members who died/ [crew names inscribed on memorial] Plinth: IN GRATEFUL REMEMBRANCE Planter plagues: (405 Squadron RCAF badge)/ THEY WILL/ NEVER GROW/ OLD Vase: RAOB
Location: Crash site on bend of road Langham Road Mumby East Lindsey Lincolnshire LN13 9SJ England
Grid Ref: TF 52690 73962
Coordinates: 53.240729010299,0.286613744184
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/78/486/large_halifax_bb216_memorial.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/78/487/large_halifax_bb216_memorial_inscription.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/78/488/large_halifax_bb216_memorial_in_context.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/78/489/large_halifax_bb216_memorial_planter_lh.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/78/490/large_halifax_bb216_memorial_planter_rh.jpg

Halifax Bomber Crash Memorial (September 4th 2004): A memorial was erected to commemorate the four airmen who died in a Halifax Bomber crash near Langham, Mumby on September 1st 1942.

Robertshaw Sisters Memorial: A plaque was installed in memory of Hilda and Bessie Robertshaw, two teachers from Mumby who drowned at Perranporth on the Cornish coast in October 1920.

A memorial to these brave airmen was erected on September 4th 2004 and can be found in Langham Lane, Mumby.

A plaque in memory of the two sisters is located in Mumby church.
narrative: On the night of 1 September 1942, Halifax BB216 of 405 (Vancouver) Squadron took off from Topcliffe, Yorkshire, bound for Saarbrücken, Germany. After crossing the English coast, the aircraft developed engine trouble; the engines caught fire, and the captain, Flight Sergeant Norman McKenzie RCAF, ordered his crew of seven to bail out. The bomber came down at Langham, near Mumby in Lincolnshire. Four crew members were killed: pilot Flight Sergeant Norman McKenzie, aged 27, along with Flight Sergeant Clarence Eagles, Flight Sergeant Louis Dawdy, aged 20, and Sergeant Harold Stone. Three others survived, including at least one who sustained injuries.
